h: Following Shakespeare from cradle to grave
p: An hour is about right for New Place, but the real joy is how neatly it fits into a walk through Shakespeare's whole life story, much of it within a few streets.

Directly across the road is the Guild Chapel, and alongside it Shakespeare's Schoolroom and Guildhall, where the young William is believed to have been taught. Standing in that room and then crossing over to the site of the grand house he bought later in life is a neat way to see how far the glover's son from Henley Street came.

Head up to Henley Street to visit Shakespeare's Birthplace, the half-timbered house where he was born and grew up. Then finish at Holy Trinity Church, down by the river, where he's buried. Between them, those stops trace his life from beginning to end, and you can walk the lot in an afternoon.

Still keen? Hall's Croft, the elegant home of his daughter Susanna and her husband Dr John Hall, is a short stroll away in the Old Town. A bit further out, Anne Hathaway's Cottage sits in the hamlet of Shottery, and Mary Arden's Farm, linked to his mother's family, is a few miles beyond at Wilmcote. Several of these are run by the Shakespeare Birthplace Trust, so look at joint tickets if you plan to do a few.

End the day by the Avon. The Royal Shakespeare Theatre and the Swan Theatre sit on the riverbank, and even if you're not seeing a show, the gardens, the boats and the swans make a lovely evening stroll.
